exposure: Absence of antiretroviral treatment for prophylaxis
cohort: The study included 4104 infants (2053 born to HIV-infected mothers and 2051 born to HIV-uninfected mothers), matched on gender and study site, enrolled during their first week of life in three referral hospitals in Cameroon.
finding: Loss to follow-up among HIV-unexposed infants was four times higher than among HIV-exposed infants, with distinct maternal, socioeconomic, and obstetrical factors associated with LTFU in each group.
mod_finding: Emergency caesarean section was independently associated with loss to follow-up among HIV-exposed infants.
